title: The Magician

seo.title: Destiny matrix 1 — The Magician: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Arcanum 1 is The Magician: will, initiative and the energy of a start. What 1 means in the destiny matrix and how a strong version differs from a weak one.
queries: meaning of arcanum 1 in the destiny matrix
what arcanum 1 stands for in the destiny matrix

meaning: The first arcanum in the destiny matrix is The Magician, the energy of pure will and of beginning. If a one came up in your calculation, this is a person who works as a source: they do not wait for circumstances to line up, they take what is at hand and set things moving themselves. “One” here is read literally — it is the point where everything only starts, not yet split into doubts, for and against.

As a number of destiny, one is about authorship. Its bearer is not satisfied with taking part: it matters to them to put their own name on the result and to see a mark in the world that would not be there without them. This is the active, “daytime” side of the matrix — not storing up, but showing; not waiting for a sign, but making the first move. Hence the character of the energy: direct, impatient, turned outwards.

On the tarot card, The Magician stands at a table with the symbols of all the elements and joins “above” and “below” with a single gesture. This is the image of a conductor: an idea turns into a thing directly, through the hand and the will, with no go-betweens and no long approvals. Being the first arcanum feels like a steady inner itch of “just do it” — a quiet pressure that looks for a way out in a concrete move rather than in thinking about it.

Strong and weak versions are one energy turned in different directions. In the strong one the will goes into the object: a person makes what did not exist and measures themselves by what is done. In the weak one it turns back on the author — it matters more to feel capable than to carry an idea through to a thing, and the force leaks away into loud intentions and plans that never become a result. The difference is not in the amount of energy but in where the will points: at the work, or at the image of oneself.

Telling one apart from its neighbouring arcana is easiest by the direction of its force. The second arcanum, The High Priestess, carries force too, but the opposite kind: she knows and stays silent, gathers inside, waits for the right moment — while The Magician shows himself outwards and acts first. And from the eleventh, Strength, one is separated by distance: The Magician is good at the dash and at the start, Strength is good at holding out and finishing what was begun. The first arcanum is about taking something on, not about seeing it through to the end.

article.title: Arcanum 1 in the destiny matrix — The Magician: meaning, calling card and talents
article.short: 1 in the destiny matrix is The Magician, the arcanum of the first step. It is the energy that turns “I want to” into “I’m doing it”: an idea takes shape by your own hands, out of what is already there, without waiting for perfect conditions. It is one of the two rarest arcana in the matrix. Among its points, 1 turns up only for people born on the first of any month — then The Magician is the calling card — or in January, when he sits in the spiritual task and opens the line of talent. In the plus, The Magician is a master: he starts, strikes deals and carries an idea through to something that works. In the minus, he is a conjurer: he puts on a show instead of doing the work, or never quite lets himself begin.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 1: The Magician — who has it and what it means
seo.description: Destiny matrix 1 is The Magician, the arcanum of the first step. Only people born on the 1st or in January have it: what it means and where it’s sought in vain.

sections.h2: What 1 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: One is where counting starts, and the card means just that: the first move. In Waite’s deck [The Fool](/encyclopedia/arcanum/22) comes before The Magician as card zero; in the matrix he is number twenty-two and closes the circle. Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, tells them apart like this: with The Fool “it is still unclear which fork the fool will choose”, while The Magician “has chosen and is acting”. After The Magician comes [The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/arcanum/2) — knowledge that stays within. The Magician is the same knowledge brought out into the open and put to work.

The key thing to grasp about this card is that **The Magician does not create out of nothing.** Wen stresses that he is “someone who creates from what already exists”. You see this in life straight away. A person with a strong 1 does not wait for the money, the time, the diploma and the right team to turn up. They look at what they have today — two free evenings, an old laptop, a friend who knows the subject — and put a first version together from that. Rough, but alive. While others are still debating how it ought to be done, they already have something to show.

The Magician’s second side is the word. In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings the card opens with “skill, diplomacy, address, subtlety”, and only later comes “self-confidence, will”. Wen links The Magician to Mercury, which in astrology is the planet of speech, trade and messages. So 1 is not just drive. It is the knack of explaining an idea so that people start to help, of reaching agreement where others argue, and of selling an idea before it has become a thing. That last one is a strength and a risk at once.

The third side is focus. Wen calls The Magician “the card of individuality” and likens it to Newton’s first law of motion: “an object in motion will stay in motion until an external force is applied to stop it”. The power of 1 runs in a single direction; spread across ten projects, it vanishes. Waite says the same thing in loftier terms: “in a very high sense it is thought, in the fixation thereof”. A thought that has stopped being a dream and become a decision.

And one last thing, without which The Magician turns into a caricature. For Waite this is a card not of personal cleverness but of “the divine motive in man”, of “the possession and communication of the Powers and Gifts of the Spirit”. His Magician is not the source of power but its conductor: the power runs through him into the work. In everyday terms, 1 works best when a person serves the work rather than their own image. Once the work becomes a stage for a flashy act, the master turns into a conjurer.

sections.h2: Who has a 1 in their matrix
paragraphs: Arcanum 1 is the only one that addition cannot produce in the matrix. Almost every point of the chart is a sum of other points, and the sum of two arcana is never less than two. Numbers above 22 are reduced by adding their digits: 23 → 5, 30 → 3, 44 → 8. Such a reduction yields 1 only from 100, and a hundred is reached only in the totals of the chakra table, where seven numbers are added at once. That is why **the arcanum of beginnings stands only in the starting points** — the places where nothing has been added yet: the day and the month of birth.

paragraphs: Altogether, 13.8% of people have a 1 somewhere in their matrix — about one in seven. We counted this across all 46,300 dates from 1 January 1900 to October 2026. Only The High Priestess is rarer (13.4%), while each of the other twenty arcana turns up in the charts of 59–85% of people. So The Magician is no mark of the chosen and no “main card” — but it is not something everyone gets either.

In every other point nobody ever has a 1: not in the centre, not in the karmic tail, not in the money or relationship lines, not in the purposes, not in the family lines. Why people sometimes “find” it there is explained below, in the section on where people look for The Magician in vain. 1 as the arcanum of the year is calculated differently and has a page of its own: [1 for the year in the destiny matrix](/year/1).

One more clarification. A 1 in the matrix is the number of a card, not a numerological “life path number”. Numerology adds all the digits of a date into one, while the matrix keeps each point separate, and each has its own role. So reading a 1 always starts with the question of where it stands.

sections.h2: 1 as the calling card: born on the first of the month
paragraphs: The calling card is point A, the birth day arcanum. It shows not the whole personality but what people notice before anything else: your pace, the way you open a conversation, the role you are handed in a new group. For anyone born on the 1st, this point holds The Magician.

From the first meeting, people read this person as someone who knows where to start. While the group is still talking, they say, “Let me sketch a draft by tonight” — and by tonight the draft exists. They speak quickly and to the point, find words easily and explain complicated things in plain language. In a new team they are soon given the role of the starter: launch the project, run the first meeting, strike a deal with the person nobody else can get through to. **The Magician’s calling card sounds like a promise: with this person, things will get moving.**

That impression has a flip side: it travels faster than the person. People decide they will cope anyway and offer no help, even when help is needed. And anyone who sees the dexterity but not yet the result starts to suspect a trick: too smooth a talker, too quick to agree. Waite’s “subtlety” is easily read as cunning. The simplest way to check your calling card is by what repeats: what different people say about you when you first meet, and what they already expect of you by the second meeting.

The calling card also leads the first decade of life: on the age scale, point A covers the years from birth to ten. A childhood under The Magician often sounds like “I can do it myself!” The child takes toys apart to see how they work, bargains with adults, takes on things they have not yet grown into. A ban sounds to them like a dare. Real errands and real tools suited to their age work better: The Magician grows when what he does is of use to someone.

Next to the calling card, in the “Character” section, stands the card of the month, point B. It decides which card works in tandem with The Magician. This is also where a curious property of 1 shows: **added to any card except The Fool, it moves that card exactly one step forward.** The decade from 10 to 20 is the sum of the day and the month, so for people born on the 1st it is always led by the card one number higher than their birth month. The Magician replaces nothing — he takes the next step.

paragraphs: The same sum sits in the emotions of Sahasrara, the top chakra, which governs the link to a bigger plan. And for people born on the 1st, the physics of that chakra is The Magician himself. The row reads “1, the month, the month plus one”: for someone born on 1 March it is 1-3-4. For you, a bigger plan is something to be done, not dreamt about. There is more on the top chakra in the article on [Sahasrara](/encyclopedia/chakra/sahasrara).

sections.h2: 1 in the line of talent and the spiritual task: born in January
paragraphs: For people born in January, The Magician stands in point B, at the top of the chart. This is the spiritual task — a quality a person learns to handle from the inside. Its energy shows early and so is easily mistaken for an inborn gift. With 1 that is exactly what happens: the readiness to take things on yourself and to pick up new skills fast is noticed early, and it is easy to take it for a ready-made talent.

But a task is wider than an ability. Nimble hands and a silver tongue are not enough. The Magician’s task in point B is to become the author of your own actions: to start without waiting to be invited or allowed, to answer for what you set going, and to use your skill honestly — for the work, not for effect. The inner question of people born in January runs something like this: “Which of the things I’ve done are truly mine?” The same point opens the sky line, and in the section on tasks of the soul The Magician comes as the first task. For January births the total of the sky line always equals the karmic task plus one: here too, 1 moves the neighbouring card one step on.

When people ask about “1 in talents”, they mean exactly the January case. The line of talent B–P–K in the “Profession and work you love” section is read like this: the first card is the raw material, the second the method, the third the result. For people born in January the raw material of talent is The Magician: hands, words, initiative, the ability to master a new tool quickly. The other two cards are built the same way for everyone born in January, and this is one of the most elegant patterns in the matrix: **both come from the centre of the chart.** The result is the centre plus one, the method is the centre plus two (if that goes above 22, the digits are added). For example, for people born on 15 January 1990 the centre is 7, The Chariot, and the line of talent is 1-9-8: The Magician, The Hermit, Justice.

Our reading: the talent of January births does not come from outside. It is their own centre — the place where they feel at home and at ease — moved one step and two steps forward. The Magician adds no borrowed abilities; he carries further what is already in a person. That is exactly how Wen describes the card: creating from what already exists.

Where does this raw material earn money without burning a person out? Wherever the start depends on you and the work of your hands and head can be seen. Launching a new line of business, prototypes and pilots, a craft with tools — from joinery to code to cooking — sales and negotiation, teaching a skill in a “watch how it’s done” way, a practice of your own. A 1 has the hardest time where for years you must carry out someone else’s initiative and the result dissolves into a shared report. Then it is worth changing not the field but the form: an accountant with a 1 comes alive when asked to build a new accounting system rather than keep the old one running.

On the age scale point B leads the third decade, so for everyone born in January the years from 20 to 30 pass under The Magician. It is a decade of firsts that are your own: the first craft, the first job where the result depends on you, the first venture started without a prompt. The main question of these years is not “What should I be?” but “What can I do on my own that someone actually needs?” The risk lies in two extremes: trying everything and mastering nothing, or waiting until thirty for the perfect start.

In the chakra table the January Magician stands in the energy of Sahasrara: what drives you towards a bigger plan is the wish to make it real, not to contemplate it. In “Character” he is paired with the birth day arcanum: born on 15 January — read [The Magician and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/1-15); born on 31 January — 31 reduces to 4, and that is [The Magician and The Emperor](/encyclopedia/combination/1-4). For January births the decade from 10 to 20 is led by the day arcanum plus one: for those born on 15 January that is 16, The Tower.

sections.h2: 1 January: two Magicians in one chart
paragraphs: 1 January is the only date in the year when 1 stands in two points at once: the calling card and the spiritual task. Two Magicians do not mean twice the willpower: the points play different roles, and what is interesting is precisely that they coincide. **What people see in you from the first meeting is exactly what you have yet to learn.**

That is the trap. The outer Magician — confident, deft, ready to take things on — is so convincing that the inner work is easy to skip. Everyone around is sure you will manage, and you start believing it instead of testing it. The task for people born on 1 January is not to let the image outrun the work: the skill others see has to be proved again and again by what actually gets done.

Their age scale is curious too. Childhood passes under The Magician, the twenties under The Magician again, and between them, from 10 to 20, every one of them without exception has The High Priestess: 1 + 1 = 2. Our reading: two decades of action divided by a decade of quiet. The teenage years may be lived inwardly — in reading, in watching, in a closed world of one’s own — and when The Magician goes out to people the second time, he comes not empty-handed but with what The High Priestess has managed to gather. The same High Priestess sits in the emotions of Sahasrara: the top chakra row for people born on 1 January is 1-1-2. For you, action and the wish to act are one and the same, and you live it quietly, without an audience.

sections.h2: Master or conjurer: The Magician in the plus and in the minus
paragraphs: First, a common misconception. A number taken from a date of birth is never reversed, and “1 in the minus” is not a special card but the same energy used the wrong way. The Magician’s plus and minus are made of one material — dexterity. The question is what it works for. It is no accident that old decks called this card the Juggler, a street conjurer. **The master and the conjurer can do the same things; the difference is what remains after the show.**

You know The Magician in the plus by what he has made. He ships the first version while others are arguing about the right one. He learns with his hands: instead of reading a fifth book on swimming, he gets into the water with a coach. He builds a team out of acquaintances, a budget out of whatever there is, time out of lunch breaks. He explains things so that people join in of their own accord, and makes deals that no side regrets later. And he leaves things behind: software people use, a stool people sit on, a course people learn from.
The minus of 1 comes in three forms, and they are opposites of one another.

ul: **A show instead of the work.** The ability to impress starts to stand in for the result: the presentation is ready before the product, the promise sounds better than the work looks later. From there it is one step to manipulation. The Magician knows well which words work on people, and in the minus he moves people rather than the work.

**The Magician who never starts.** The opposite tilt, and just as common. The skill is there, the tools are there, but the person waits for permission: one more course, one more certificate, a little more preparation. In a reading, Wen takes The Magician reversed as “an external force that has been applied to stop that advancing movement”. Often that force is someone else’s voice in your own head: “Who are you to start?”

**Doing it all alone.** Competence turns into loneliness. Tasks are not handed over because “it’s quicker to do it myself”; help is not asked for because nobody offers it anyway. The work hits the ceiling of one person’s two hands.

paragraphs: How do you tell the master from the conjurer in yourself? **A trick works only while no one can see how it is done. A craft works even when you show how.** If you would feel awkward letting the other person see how you won their agreement, it was a trick.

sections.h2: What to do if you have a 1 in your matrix

ol: **Start with what you have today.** Not with a plan but with a first version: what can you make in one evening with the hands, money and people you already have? The Magician spends more strength waiting for the right conditions than on the work itself.

**Show what you’ve done, not what you’ve planned.** A 1 has a strong way with words, and that is the catch: an idea you have already talked about has had its share of admiration, and you feel less like doing it. Speak when you have something to show.
**Go deep into one craft.** The Magician grows as a master, and mastery is a tool learned so well that the hands know more than the head. Ten shallow skills make not a master but a conjurer.
**Test your methods for transparency.** Before an important conversation, ask yourself: would I be happy for the other person to see exactly how I am persuading them? If not, change the method.

**Hand over part of the work.** For a 1 this is not weakness but the move from a one-man act to a venture with more than two hands. A simple test: what would be left of your project if you went away for a month?

sections.h2: Where people look for The Magician in vain: the centre, tails, compatibility
paragraphs: **1 in the centre of the matrix.** The centre never holds a 1. The centre is the sum of the four main points of the chart, and, as we have seen, addition does not produce a 1. If some calculator has put a 1 in your centre — or in your calling card although you were born on the 23rd — it reduces large numbers by subtracting 22: 23 − 22 = 1. In the classic scheme this site uses, the digits are added: 23 → 2 + 3 = 5. Recalculate your date and read whichever card lands in the centre.

**The “Dark Magician”.** That is not 1. Popular readings use the name for the karmic tail 18-6-15 — The Moon, The Lovers and The Devil — and it has its own detailed page: [karmic tail 18-6-15](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-15). 1 never appears in the karmic tail, nor in the programs that repeat in circles. The same goes for the other “magical” names: “The Wizard” is [9-9-18](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-9-18), the “Magical Victim” is [9-18-9](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-18-9), love magic is [18-6-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-6-6). Every one of these tails contains The Moon, the card of mystery and reflected light, and not one contains The Magician. The magic of the popular programs is about spells and secrets; 1 is about craft.

**Compatibility.** In the couple’s matrix, where the matching points of two people are added together, 1 never comes up either. If both partners have The Magician in the same point — both born on the 1st or both in January — the couple will have a 2 there, The High Priestess: two Magicians together give not double the drive but quiet. Which arcana occur in a couple is covered in the section [“Arcana in compatibility”](/encyclopedia/compatibility). And how The Magician gets on with other arcana within one personal matrix is covered on the combination pages — from [The Magician and The High Priestess](/encyclopedia/combination/1-2) to [The Magician and The Fool](/encyclopedia/combination/1-22).

sections.h2: Waite’s Magician: the gesture, the table and the sign of infinity
paragraphs: The best-known image of this card comes from the deck of Arthur Edward Waite, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith and published in 1909. In The Pictorial Key to the Tarot Waite describes “a youthful figure in the robe of a magician, having the countenance of divine Apollo, with smile of confidence and shining eyes”. He stands before a table, and almost every detail here means something.

**The gesture.** The right hand raises a wand towards heaven; the left points to the earth. According to Waite, this “dual sign is known in very high grades of the Instituted Mysteries” and shows “the descent of grace, virtue and light, drawn from things above and derived to things below”. Wen reads the gesture as the Hermetic formula “As Above, So Below”: “every plane of consciousness and every level of existence is interconnected”.

**The table.** On it lie the symbols of the four Tarot suits — wand, cup, sword and pentacle. Waite calls them “the elements of natural life, which lie like counters before the adept, and he adapts them as he wills”. This is where Wen draws the conclusion on which this whole article rests: The Magician creates from what already exists, not from nothing.

**The sign of infinity and the serpent.** Above the magician’s head is a figure 8 lying on its side — for Waite, “the mysterious sign of the Holy Spirit, the sign of life”. His belt is a serpent devouring its own tail. Usually that is a symbol of eternity, but here, Waite specifies, it means “the eternity of attainment in the spirit”.

**Roses and lilies.** Flowers grow below. Waite recognises in them a line from the Song of Songs, flos campi and lilium convallium, “the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys” — only here the wild flowers are “changed into garden flowers, to shew the culture of aspiration”. For 1 this may be the most precise image of all: an impulse is worth nothing until it has been cultivated, like a garden.

**The Juggler.** Waite knew the card had another face. In older decks the first trump showed a conjurer — in the French, Marseille tradition he is Le Bateleur, a fairground trickster. Waite lists him as “the Magus, Magician, or Juggler, the caster of the dice and mountebank, in the world of vulgar trickery” and dismisses this as “the colportage interpretation”, a pedlar’s reading far from the true meaning of the symbol. In the same passage he quotes Éliphas Lévi: the Magus signifies “that unity which is the mother of numbers”. The one from which all counting begins.

In readings, Waite made this card stand for “the Querent, if male”. That has nothing to do with the matrix: gender does not change a single number in the calculation, and for women a 1 reads exactly the same. Nor is there a reversed position in the matrix — instead, people speak of the energy in the plus and in the minus.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: Meaning of the card: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (text of the 1922 reissue), and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Both are quoted in their original English.
Compatibility: Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024).

Calculation: the classic destiny matrix scheme, with numbers reduced by adding their digits, as in this site’s calculator. All shares and patterns were checked by running through 46,300 dates from 1 January 1900 to 6 October 2026.

The reading of the positions, the rule that 1 moves a card one step forward, the January line of talent and the age scale of 1 January are our interpretation based on these sources. This is a symbolic reading, not a forecast of events.
